12.0 MEASURES OF CENTRAL TENDENCY
12.1 Measures of Central Tendencies
12.1.1 Determine the mode, mean and median of a set of ungrouped data.
12.1.2 Make conclusions about the effect of changes in a set of data to the value of mode, mean and median.

12.1.6 Determine mode, mean and median from data representations.
12.1.7 Apply the understanding of measures of central tendencies to make predictions, form convincing arguments and make conclusions.

13.1 Experimental Probability
13.1.1 Perform simple probability experiments, and hence state the ratio (frequency of an event/number of trials) as the experimental probability of an event.

13.3.1 Describe the complement of an event in words and by using set notations.
13.3.2 Determine the probability of the complement of an event.
